description:
We are EpochLoom.

What drew us to the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge is a simple question anyone can ask when looking at two images of the same patch of sky. What moved?

With EpochLoom, we’re building a web tool that lets anyone pick a region of the sky, flip between SPHEREx observations taken at different times, and spot changes for themselves.
summary:
EpochLoom is a public web tool that helps researchers and citizen scientists detect changes and track moving objects in NASA’s SPHEREx observations.

Built for the “Planet X and SPHEREx” challenge, it aligns images from different visits in one workspace.

Users can blink between observations, compare difference images, search for movers, inspect spectra, and share results.

NASA’s SPHEREx data powers the experience, while supporting surveys and catalogues help identify objects and assess their motion.
details:
We developed EpochLoom, a public-facing web tool that turns NASA’s SPHEREx observations into an interactive view of the changing infrared sky.

Addressing the “Planet X and SPHEREx” challenge, it aligns observations from different visits so users can compare images, detect changes, investigate moving objects, and inspect their spectra in one workspace.

EpochLoom combines SPHEREx data from NASA’s IRSA archive and AWS with supporting surveys and catalogues to help researchers assess candidates.

Instead of downloading entire image files, it retrieves only the required regions, processes requests in parallel, and caches results.

Our field-loading benchmark took 22 seconds compared with 212 seconds for whole-file downloads, reducing waiting time by approximately 90%.

By simplifying data preparation and bringing visual comparison, motion searches, measurements, and shareable results together, EpochLoom helps researchers spend more time investigating the sky.

It also makes real astronomical data more accessible to students, educators, and citizen scientists.
